quizName: DMV Practice Test #8 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs are white with red and black markings. They tell drivers about traffic laws. This sign means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: When changing lanes:

options.text: Your mirrors can adequately show you your surroundings.
Do a head check in addition to using your mirrors.
Activate your turn signal and immediately move to the right or left.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do a head check in addition to using your mirrors.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles have blind spots, just like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check your blind spot before changing lanes, in addition to using your mirrors.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that a stop sign is coming.

questions.question: Which brake is more powerful on a motorcycle?
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of the motorcycle's stopping power.

questions.question: Before starting a turn, a motorcyclist should change gears to:

options.text: Prevent a change in power in the middle of the turn.
Be able to keep both hands on the handle grips during the turn.
Prevent the motorcycle from slowing down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent a change in power in the middle of the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you turn. Shifting gears while turning can cause a sudden change in power to the rear wheel, which may cause a skid.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle:

options.text: The mirrors provide a perfect view.
The mirrors do not show your blind spots.
The mirrors should not be used, except when parking.

questions.correctAnswerText: The mirrors do not show your blind spots.
questions.explanation: Motorcycle mirrors have blind spots, like any vehicle. Always turn your head to check for traffic in your blind spot before changing lanes.

questions.question: There may be less traction available for braking when:

options.text: A motorcycle is straight up and down.
A motorcycle is on dry pavement.

questions.explanation: When a motorcycle is leaning, such as in a turn, there is less traction for braking. You can still use both brakes while turning, but you must do so carefully.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions. This sign warns that traffic is merging ahead.

questions.question: When riding at night, maintain a minimum following distance of:
questions.explanation: It is harder to judge distances in the dark. Keep a following distance of at least three seconds when riding at night.

questions.question: Stopping in a turn can be difficult because:

options.text: There is decreased traction available for stopping while the bike is leaning.
The rider is usually focused on the turn and not on the braking.
The brake controls do not work in turns.

questions.correctAnswerText: There is decreased traction available for stopping while the bike is leaning.
questions.explanation: You can use both brakes while turning, but it requires great care. When the motorcycle is leaning, some traction is used for the turn. This leaves less traction for braking.

questions.question: A motorcycle's horn is ________ a passenger vehicle's horn.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle horn is not as loud as other vehicle horns. Use your horn when needed, but do not rely on it alone to stay safe.

questions.question: When buying a motorcycle helmet, you should care most about the helmet's:
questions.explanation: Protection is the most important thing to think about when choosing a motorcycle helmet.

questions.question: Under normal conditions, a motorcyclist should stay at least ________ behind the vehicle ahead.
questions.explanation: Keep at least a two-second gap behind other vehicles when conditions are normal. When conditions are not perfect, increase this gap.

questions.question: When approaching an intersection, a motorcyclist should not:

options.text: Choose a lane position that makes them more visible.
Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
Cover the clutch and brakes to react faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Speed up to cross the intersection quickly.
questions.explanation: As you approach an intersection, choose a lane position that other drivers can see. Get your clutch and brakes ready to react fast. Slow down when entering an intersection. Do not change speed or position suddenly, as this may confuse other drivers.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a potential problem?

options.text: A change in road surface ahead
Conditions that stay the same as you approach

questions.correctAnswerText: Conditions that stay the same as you approach
questions.explanation: Watch for potential problems on the road. Plan how to reduce the risk from these hazards.

questions.question: You should flash your brake light to:

options.text: Tell other drivers you are riding near them.
Help other drivers see your motorcycle in slow traffic.
Warn other drivers you are slowing down or stopping unexpectedly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Warn other drivers you are slowing down or stopping unexpectedly.
questions.explanation: Use your brake lights to communicate with other drivers. Flash your brake light before making a sharp, fast turn off a high-speed road. Also flash it when slowing down in places where drivers may not expect you to slow down.

questions.question: Which of the following is a slippery surface?
questions.explanation: Traction is poor on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement; gravel roads; lane markings; and metal plates or utility hole covers.

questions.question: If your front wheel locks while stopping, you should:

options.text: Release the front brake and use only the rear brake.
Release the front brake right away, then press it firmly again.

questions.correctAnswerText: Release the front brake right away, then press it firmly again.
questions.explanation: If your front wheel locks during braking, release the front brake immediately and then apply it firmly again. Use both front and rear brakes when you need to stop quickly.

questions.question: If you need to react to a hazard in the road, do NOT:

options.text: Fail to communicate with other drivers.
Use your horn, lights, or signals.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fail to communicate with other drivers.
questions.explanation: Communicate with other drivers using your horn, lights, and signals. Adjust your speed to match the situation. Change your lane position or direction if needed.

questions.question: When the lights on a railroad crossing sign are flashing, what should you do?

options.text: Stop and wait until the train passes.
Go slowly and look both ways.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop and wait until the train passes.
questions.explanation: When you see flashing lights at a railroad crossing, stop completely and wait. Do not cross until the train has passed and the lights stop flashing. Never try to beat a train across the tracks.

questions.question: When you carry a load on a motorcycle, it should be:

options.text: Placed on the gas tank in front of you.
Piled against the back support or frame behind the seat.

questions.explanation: Keep loads over or in front of the rear axle. Only experienced riders should carry loads on a motorcycle.

questions.question: When turning, you should:

options.text: Move your knees away from the gas tank.
Turn only your head to look through the turn.
Turn your head and shoulders to look through the turn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn only your head to look through the turn.
questions.explanation: When turning, look where you want to go. Turn only your head, not your shoulders. Keep your eyes level with the horizon. Turning your shoulders may cause you to lose your intended path.

questions.question: Riding on ______ may provide poor traction.
questions.explanation: Poor traction can occur on wet, snowy, icy, or muddy pavement. It can also occur on gravel, lane markings, steel plates, and utility hole covers.

questions.question: Your lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to be seen.
Invite other drivers into your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Invite other drivers into your lane.
questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you be seen and avoid hazards. It should discourage other drivers from sharing your lane and give you an escape route if danger appears.

questions.question: To be seen more easily by other drivers, you should:
questions.explanation: Wearing bright clothing makes it easier for other drivers to see you. This works any time of day.
